intl.title: PennWest - International undergraduate admissions (how to apply, deadlines, English scores)

se004.title: PennWest Procedure SE004 - Undergraduate Admissions (last updated 2026-04-02)

faq.title: PennWest - International admissions FAQs (financial aid for international students)

test_policy.notes: SAT/ACT scores are optional: first-year applicants need a 2.50 cumulative GPA (weighted or unweighted) and may submit scores; admissions also reviews course trends, rigor, leadership and activities. Applicants with a 2.0-2.49 GPA may be admitted through the Compass Program, which is open to international first-year applicants. International applicants need a 2.50 GPA as determined by AACRAO Edge or a NACES credential evaluation.

requirements.notes: Apply with the PennWest online application, the Common App or a paper application; the policy says all applicants pay the $35 fee, waivable by staff. International first-year applicants submit an official high school transcript showing at least a 2.50 GPA (credential evaluated), proof of English proficiency and passport information. Financial and immigration documents (financial guarantee statement, affidavit of support, passport copy) are collected after admission for the I-20. International applicants are not eligible for provisional admission. Essay, recommendations and activities are optional per the international page.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: The page says June 1 for a fall semester start (November 1 for spring); no year is printed, so June 1 is assumed to mean 2027 for fall 2027. Applications are decided once all documents are received; the page does not say whether admission is rolling.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required for applicants whose primary language of instruction is not English. Besides the tests below, accepted evidence includes ITEP Academic 3.5, ISTEP 60, SAT EBRW 500, ACT English 21, A-Level/IGCSE/GCSE/O-Level English C, IB English 5, completion of ELS Level 112 or a campus-based ESL program at an accredited U.S. college. Exempt: a degree from a U.S. or English-medium institution, 24 credits at a U.S./English-medium college, 2+ years at a U.S. high school, an IB diploma, or citizens of listed English-speaking countries (e.g. UK, Ireland, Australia, Canada except Quebec, Nigeria, Singapore, South Africa). The international page lists TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, Pearson, GTEC CBT and STEP-EIKEN.

english.notes: IELTS Academic with no sub-score below 5.5 (SE004). Edinboro's own pages have listed IELTS 6.0, so confirm with the campus.
Pearson PTE Academic, per SE004 (not shown on the international page's minimums).

aid.notes: The international pages say students may be eligible for financial aid, scholarships, grants and student employment, and that first-year international students are eligible for housing and need-based scholarships (no amounts). The FAQ describes an undergraduate academic scholarship (minimum 2.5 GPA, kept while a 2.5 GPA is maintained) that reduces tuition to the rate non-resident Pennsylvanians pay; its dollar value is not given and the 2026-27 tuition page lists one combined out-of-state/international rate.

majors.notes: Minimum 3.0 high school GPA and grades of B or higher in algebra I/II or calculus, biology and chemistry. A separate Associate of Science in Nursing needs a 2.75 GPA and a proficient ATI TEAS score (SE004).
